questions.question: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity parallel to the field. The path of the particle is: (A) circular (B) helical (C) straight line (D) parabolic
questions.solution:
Magnetic force $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B}$ is zero when $\vec{v}\parallel\vec{B}$ because $\sin\theta = \sin 0 = 0$.

With no magnetic force the particle continues in a straight line with unchanged speed. Answer (C). (If $\vec{v}$ had a component across the field, that component would give a helix.)

questions.question: A galvanometer of resistance $100\,\Omega$ gives full-scale deflection for $1\,\mathrm{mA}$. To convert it into a voltmeter of range $0$–$10\,\mathrm{V}$, the series resistance required is: (A) $100\,\Omega$ (B) $1000\,\Omega$ (C) $9900\,\Omega$ (D) $10000\,\Omega$
questions.solution:
For full-scale current, $R_g + R = \frac{V}{I_g} = \frac{10}{1\times10^{-3}} = 10{,}000\,\Omega$.

$R = 10{,}000 - 100 = 9900\,\Omega$. Answer (C). A high series resistance limits the current through the coil to $I_g$ even at full voltage.

questions.question: Using Biot–Savart's law, obtain the magnetic flux density at a point near a long straight current-carrying conductor. A long wire carries $10\,\mathrm{A}$; find the field at $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ from it.
questions.solution:
Biot–Savart's law: $d\vec{B} = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\frac{I\,d\vec{l}\times\hat{r}}{r^2}$. For an element at distance $x$ along a long wire, the perpendicular distance being $a$, integrating over both directions gives

$B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}\left[\sin\theta_1 + \sin\theta_2\right] \xrightarrow[\text{long wire}]{}\ B = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}$.

Numerical: $B = \frac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 10}{2\pi \times 0.05} = \frac{2\times10^{-6} \times 10}{0.05} = 4\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{T}$.

The field lines are concentric circles around the wire, with direction given by the right-hand grip rule.

questions.question: Derive an expression for the force per unit length between two infinitely long parallel straight conductors carrying currents $I_1$ and $I_2$. Hence define one ampere.
questions.solution:
The first wire produces at the second (distance $d$) a field $B_1 = \frac{\mu_0 I_1}{2\pi d}$, perpendicular to both the wire and the separation.

Force on length $l$ of the second wire: $F = B_1 I_2 l$, so the force per unit length is $\frac{F}{l} = \frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$.

By Newton's third law the first wire experiences an equal and opposite force. Currents in the same direction attract; in opposite directions they repel.

Definition: one ampere is that steady current which, flowing in each of two infinitely long parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed one metre apart in vacuum, produces between them a force of $2\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{N}$ per metre of length.

questions.question: Show that the torque on a rectangular current loop in a uniform magnetic field is $\tau = NIAB\sin\theta$. Why is the magnetic field in a moving-coil galvanometer made radial?
questions.solution:
Take a rectangular coil with $N$ turns, sides $l$ and $b$, carrying current $I$ in a field $B$, with the normal to the coil at angle $\theta$ to $\vec{B}$. The two sides of length $l$ carry opposite currents, so the forces $F = NBIl$ on them are equal, opposite and separated by $b\sin\theta$; they form a couple.

Torque: $\tau = F \times$ perpendicular distance $= NBIl\,(b\sin\theta) = NIAB\sin\theta$, with $A = lb$. In vector form $\vec{\tau} = N I \vec{A}\times\vec{B}$.

A radial field keeps the plane of the coil always parallel to the field lines, so $\theta = 90^\circ$ for every deflection and the torque $NIAB$ is constant. Then the deflection is directly proportional to the current, giving a uniformly divided linear scale.

questions.question: (a) Describe a cyclotron with a labelled sketch and derive the expression for the cyclotron frequency. (b) A cyclotron accelerates protons with a magnetic field of $1.5\,\mathrm{T}$. Find the frequency of the alternating voltage and the maximum energy of protons emerging from a dee of radius $0.5\,\mathrm{m}$. Take $m_p = 1.67\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
questions.solution:
(a) Two hollow D-shaped electrodes (dees) are placed in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to their plane, with a high-frequency alternating voltage across the gap. A particle injected at the centre is bent into a semicircle inside a dee; crossing the gap it is accelerated, and the larger radius keeps the period the same, so the same frequency continues to work.

Derivation: the magnetic force supplies the centripetal force, $qvB = \frac{mv^2}{r}$, so $v = \frac{qBr}{m}$ and the period is $T = \frac{2\pi r}{v} = \frac{2\pi m}{qB}$ — independent of speed and radius. Cyclotron frequency $f = \frac{1}{T} = \frac{qB}{2\pi m}$.

(b) $f = \frac{(1.6\times10^{-19})(1.5)}{2\pi(1.67\times10^{-27})} = \frac{2.4\times10^{-19}}{1.05\times10^{-26}} \approx 2.3\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{Hz} = 23\,\mathrm{MHz}$.

Maximum speed at the outer edge: $v = \frac{qBr}{m} = \frac{(1.6\times10^{-19})(1.5)(0.5)}{1.67\times10^{-27}} = 7.2\times10^{7}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.

Maximum kinetic energy: $K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.5 \times 1.67\times10^{-27} \times (7.2\times10^7)^2 \approx 4.3\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm{J} \approx 27\,\mathrm{MeV}$.

Limitation: relativistic mass increase makes the period drift at high speeds, so synchrocyclotrons or synchrotrons are used above about $20\,\mathrm{MeV}$ for protons.
